title: Compact GPU bootstrap phases and dynamic kernel multipath
creator: Aisha Goyal
description: Reduce runtime startup jitter and simplify GPU dependency graph by splitting bootstrap into deterministic phases, adding a compact probe cache, and introducing a dynamic kernel multipath loader that picks compatible kernel bundles at runtime. This ticket consolidates several ad-hoc heuristics scattered across the runtime into a single, testable pipeline: 1) environment detection (driver/cu* versions), 2) capability classification (compute capability, tensor core availability, memory topology), 3) candidate kernel selection (preferred stable bundles, quantized variants), 4) resolved-loader handshake with fallback policy. Goal: lower cold-start latency variance by 20% for mixed GPU fleets and shrink the runtime dependency surface to make upgrades (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS) less risky.
comments: 2026-02-12 — Initial spike complete: validated that splitting probe into ‘fast-detect’ and ‘deep-validate’ reduces median probe time by ~35ms on p4d nodes. Spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/gpu-bootstrap-spike

2026-02-18 — Design doc posted: 'Dynamic Kernel Multipath Loader' (link in PR description). Asked for review from runtime and infra owners. @Jin Park requested concrete SLO rollback criteria and a canary plan.

2026-02-25 — Architectural review: agreed to implement a compact probe cache persisted in instance local disk with eviction TTL to avoid repeated heavy symbol checks. Concern flagged: cache poisoning if driver updates mid-boot — added integrity check step (signature of kernel-bundle meta).

2026-03-03 — Engineering update: landed prototype branch eng/246783/bootstrap-phases. Basic multipath selection works and falls back to generic cuBLAS path when CUTLASS symbol lookup fails. Benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567

2026-03-08 — QA notes: intermittent failure on heterogeneous test bed where mixed driver versions trigger a nonfatal warning but downstream perf regressions for small batch sizes. Reproduced locally, adding extra compatibility shim for half-precision dispatch.

2026-03-12 — PM review: Marco verified rollout checklist. Plan: staged canary across 5% of Dedicated and Private fleets, monitor probe latency, kernel-miss rate, and cold-start failure SLI. If kernel-miss > 0.5% or cold-start error > 0.1%, automatic rollback.
